proposed_from.topic: Sharp sign-ratio closure and singularity-robust inference for multi-setting OVB bounds. Audit Huntington-Klein 2026 and released hetset 0.1.0: replace the bias-difference LP by the sharp componentwise union P+ or P- implied by positive bounded bias ratios; prove converse attainability, log-cycle/Farkas certificates, exact branch-LP or MILP computation, an unconditional support relaxation gap, and exact requested-pin gaps. Construct feasible confidence sets uniformly valid at zero bias, branch/basis ties, and n^(-1/2)-weak supershort ratio denominators using numerical-delta inference off singularities and undivided primitive-moment inversion near them, with pointwise oracle recovery in regular regions. Reimplement R/Python/Stata routines and reanalyse ACS returns-to-college pinning. Do not stop at the counterexample, routine sign enumeration, or generic projection inference.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: {"published_axis":"The closest result is HuntingtonKlein2026, Proposition 4 on p. 13. It proves only that the effect vector belongs to a polytope built from separately extremized bias differences, even though Assumption 3 on pp. 8--9 requires one positive-ratio bias vector and notes the induced common sign and transitivity. Theorem 1 gives the affine image of one positive or negative polyhedron per connected component and adds a joint-margin-preserving observationally equivalent Gaussian augmentation; equality is claimed only on that nonsingular Gaussian family, while arbitrary laws retain containment. Theorem 3 gives a symbolic strict support gap on every \\(a>0\\), \\(R>1\\) in its two-setting family; Theorem 4 gives an exact pin gap; and Theorem 5 solves a three-setting equality cycle with a zero stratum and two simultaneous pins. Definition 3 on p. 15 contains none of these slice characterizations. Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18 motivates the project-maintained polynomial sensitivity region. Theorem 6 adds a separate pointwise regular-cell result: stable winning branches and primal--dual bases make its directional endpoint map \\(C^1\\), yield a Gaussian limit, and make Hong--Li numerical-delta endpoint intervals first-order equivalent to the known-cell oracle. ChernozhukovEtAl2026 is the nearest OVB sharpness and efficiency paper, but its target is a single-setting bound and it imposes no cross-setting multiplicative compatibility. KitamuraStoye2018 and GalichonHenry2011 contribute transferable primal--dual compatibility methods, not an OVB sign-union theorem. KaidoMolinariStoye2019, FangSantos2019, HongLi2018, and BolducKhalafYelou2010 separately cover projection, directional maps, numerical derivatives, and ratios; none states this multi-setting closure or regular-cell endpoint result.","repo_axis":"The closest archived proposals contribute reusable proof motifs but no result on Huntington--Klein or multi-setting OVB ratios. The accepted partial-transport run supplies full-law endpoint attainment; the collider-bias run identifies open-set separation from rectangular relaxations; the BudgetIV run records unresolved exact cycle and weak-ratio topology; and the data-fusion run leaves tie-uniform numerical-delta inference open. This core does not treat those claims as proved. It instantiates their missing common-witness lesson at a new published target and makes the exact sign closure, strict support gap, and undivided supershort relation explicit."}

seed_details.one_line: Sharp componentwise sign-ratio closure with latent Gaussian attainability and a nondegenerate support-function gap from the Huntington--Klein polytope.
seed_details.anchor_location: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 3, Proposition 4, Proposition 6, and the common-sign remark on pp. 12--17.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separate extrema of \(D^{jk}=(\rho^{jk}-1)B^k\) by one globally compatible bias vector, then prove the reverse inclusion by an observationally equivalent latent completion.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from HuntingtonKlein2026 because positive ratios visibly imply common signs.
seed_details.rebuttal: Common sign gives only necessity; the missing content is the componentwise union for an arbitrary sparse graph, pointwise latent attainability, an exact support gap, pin slices, and uniform inference based on the sharp rather than relaxed set.

seed_details.one_line: Uniform primitive-moment inversion for supershort-calibrated sharp OVB sets at zero and \(n^{-1/2}\)-weak coefficient changes, with regular-region numerical-delta recovery.
seed_details.anchor_location: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 4, the supershort limitations paragraph on pp. 21--22, and the inference limitation in the Conclusion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Keep numerator and denominator moments undivided inside the test inversion because the ratio and sign maps cease to be continuous on the local zero-denominator experiment.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from generic projection or Fieller inference because one can always project a confidence ellipsoid for primitive moments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic projection does not supply the closure-correct supershort constraint, simultaneous sign branches and LP bases, a feasible sharp-set solver, or a uniform switch that recovers numerical-delta oracle length in separated regions.
seed_details.status: survived as the inference rung and open frontier

seed_details.one_line: Closure-complete log-cycle and Farkas certificates for sparse ratio graphs, including the all-zero stratum and exact branch-LP or MILP equivalence.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Stratify before taking logs, because \(x_i=\log|B_i|\) is exact on a nonzero sign branch but deletes the all-zero closure face.

seed_details.rebuttal: The positive-stratum cycle test is classical, but its equivalence to the original OVB union with box faces, componentwise zeros, pins, and an exact MILP is not supplied by the graph result and is needed as the identification certificate.

seed_details.rebuttal: LP syntax is routine, but the exact union slice, simultaneous latent attainability, pin-status trichotomy, and symbolic gap from the published outer pin are not.

proposed_from.literature_map: HuntingtonKlein2026 is the direct anchor. Its Introduction motivates cross-setting sensitivity analysis, Assumption 3 states \(B^j=\rho^{jk}B^k\) with a positive bounded ratio, the discussion immediately after Assumption 3 acknowledges the common-sign and zero-bias implications, Proposition 4 gives only containment of the two-setting effect vector in a bias-difference polytope, Proposition 6 intersects those pairwise containments for \(K\) settings, Definition 4 performs pinning in that outer polytope, and the Conclusion identifies sampling inference as absent. No converse or sharpness theorem appears. BalkePearl1997, Sections 2--3, supplies the latent-response linear-programming and endpoint-attainment pattern: validity of an optimization bound is paired with compatible latent laws attaining its extrema. KitamuraStoye2018, Theorem 3.1 and Section 4, supplies the primal finite-cone representation and its dual half-space logic, including equality faces; the present graph problem changes the first reduction because positive ratios create a union of sign polyhedra and logarithms omit the zero stratum. GalichonHenry2011, Theorems 1--3, supplies finite compatibility inequalities and dual separation as an identification device. KaidoMolinariStoye2019, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 3.1, supplies calibrated projection with uniform coverage for finite moment equality and inequality models, but assumes a regular moment representation and does not treat estimated ratio maps at zero. FangSantos2019, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3, establishes that a Gaussian first stage does not rescue an ordinary bootstrap at merely directionally differentiable maps and motivates derivative-aware resampling at branch or basis ties. HongLi2018, Section 3, supplies numerical finite-perturbation estimation of directional derivatives, but its uniform result covers convex Lipschitz maps rather than a discontinuous ratio calibration. BolducKhalafYelou2010, Sections 2--3, inverts joint tests for several numerator--denominator primitives and permits unbounded Fieller regions. Dufour1997, Theorems 3.1--3.3, rules out uniformly valid always-bounded inference for an unbounded locally almost unidentified ratio. ChernozhukovEtAl2026, Theorems 2--4, gives sharp single-setting omitted-variable-bias bounds and efficient estimation of observed bound components, but has no cross-setting multiplicative closure. Searches by title, forward-citation metadata, and the target--method pairs \(\text{multi-setting OVB}+\text{sign union}\), \(\text{OVB ratio graph}+\text{cycle certificate}\), and \(\text{supershort ratio}+\text{Fieller inversion}\) found no closer paper through September 2026.

accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Reverse attainment and equality are conditional on the stated nonsingular jointly Gaussian observed-law submodel; arbitrary observed laws receive containment only.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Sharp over the stated jointly Gaussian observed-law family, with unrestricted admissible cross-setting covariance; not universal non-Gaussian sharpness.
